items.title: GDP, second estimate (Q3)
items.analysis: GDP came in at 4.3% against a 3.5% forecast, above expectations. The previous reading was 3.4%. The real GDP, annualized reading was the highest since Q3 2023.
items.context: Headline U.S. GDP growth is annualized. Subsequent estimates add data and may revise the same quarter.

items.title: Initial jobless claims (moved to Wednesday for Thanksgiving)
items.analysis: Jobless claims came in at 189K against a 201K forecast, below expectations. The previous reading was 203K, revised to 202K. 4-week average 196K (previous 198K); Continuing claims 1.70M (previous 1.79M). The initial claims reading was the lowest since week to Jul 18.
items.context: Initial claims count new unemployment insurance applications. The four-week average smooths weekly swings.

items.title: PCE inflation · Personal income and outlays (Oct)
items.analysis: Core PCE came in at 0.3% against a 0.3% forecast, in line with expectations. The previous reading was 0.3%. PCE m/m 0.3% (previous 0.5%); Core PCE y/y 3.3% (previous 3.1%); Personal spending m/m 0.3% (previous 0.6%).
items.context: The Fed measures its inflation target using headline PCE. Core PCE helps identify the underlying trend.

items.title: Initial jobless claims
items.analysis: Jobless claims came in at 203K against a 198K forecast, above expectations. The previous reading was 200K, revised to 202K. 4-week average 198K (previous 196K); Continuing claims 1.76M (previous 1.69M). The initial claims reading was the highest since week to Sep 5.
items.context: Initial claims count new unemployment insurance applications. The four-week average smooths weekly swings.

items.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, October 27-28, 2026
items.context: Meeting minutes show which risks officials weighed when they made the decision.
items.analysis: With regard to the outlook for monetary policy in the months ahead, almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective. Some participants expressed concern that more widespread price pressures in the context of a prolonged period of above-target inflation could increase the risk of elevated inflation becoming entrenched in the inflation expectations of households and businesses. Dissent: Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

items.title: Retail sales (Oct)
items.analysis: Retail sales came in at 0.2% against a 0.2% forecast, in line with expectations. The previous reading was 0.8%.
items.context: Retail sales are reported in dollars. Changes can reflect prices as well as the volume of goods sold.

items.title: PPI producer prices (Oct)
items.analysis: PPI came in at 0.3% against a 0.4% forecast, below expectations. The previous reading was 1.3%, revised to 1.4%.
items.context: PPI tracks prices received by producers. Some components feed into the PCE inflation calculation.

items.title: Federal Reserve announces revised tentative schedule of Federal Open Market Committee meetings in 2027
items.context: The published meeting calendar gives the timing of policy decisions and minutes.

items.title: Initial jobless claims
items.analysis: Jobless claims came in at 200K against a 195K forecast, above expectations. The previous reading was 189K, revised to 191K.
items.context: Initial claims count new unemployment insurance applications. The four-week average smooths weekly swings.

items.title: CPI inflation (Oct)
items.analysis: Core CPI came in at 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast, above expectations. The previous reading was 0.3%.
items.context: Core CPI excludes food and energy. Comparing it with headline CPI helps identify where prices changed.

items.title: Non-farm payrolls · Employment situation (Oct)
items.analysis: Payrolls came in at 165K against a 65K forecast, above expectations. The previous reading was 29K, revised to 60K.
items.context: Payrolls count jobs, while the unemployment rate comes from a separate household survey. The two measures can diverge.

items.title: Bank rate increased to 4% - November 2026 Monetary Policy Summary and Minutes
items.context: Bank Rate is the UK policy rate. The vote split shows how much agreement there was on the decision.

items.title: ECB wage tracker suggests slightly higher wage growth in first three quarters of 2027 compared with the full year of 2026
items.context: The ECB wage tracker follows negotiated pay, which can move differently from average earnings across the economy.

items.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
items.context: The Fed sets a target range for overnight interest rates. The statement explains the committee's reasoning and any dissent.
items.analysis: The Fed decided to maintain its target range at 3-3/4% to 4%.
